entry.title: From NC State to the Moon: An Aspiring Astronaut Interviews NASA Astronaut Christina Koch

media:group.media:title: From NC State to the Moon: An Aspiring Astronaut Interviews NASA Astronaut Christina Koch
media:group.media:description:
What does it really take to become a NASA astronaut? From building trust in zero gravity and balancing hobbies like rock climbing and surfing, to dealing with imposter syndrome and navigating career choices, Christina Koch shares advice for aspiring astronauts everywhere.
Koch visited NC State University, her alma mater, in August 2026 for a celebration of her return from the Artemis II mission. As part of the celebration, NC State announced that Engineering Building II would be renamed Christina Hammock Koch Hall. Just a few hours later, NC State senior Raina Gandhi sat down for this interview with Koch at Hunt Library.
🚀About Christina Koch Christina Hammock Koch is a NASA astronaut and three-time NC State alumna with degrees in electrical engineering and physics. As a mission specialist on NASA's Artemis II mission, she made history as the first woman to travel around the moon.
🎓About Your Host Raina Gandhi is a senior at NC State University double-majoring in mechanical engineering and psychology. She is a D1 student-athlete on the NC State gymnastics team and a two-time NASA intern.
🔗 Learn More Around the Moon and Pack Again events: https://news.ncsu.edu/2026/08/around-the-moon-and-pack-again/
Recapping Christina Koch’s visit to NC State: https://news.ncsu.edu/2026/08/a-new-name-at-home/

entry.title: Christina Koch Visits NC State University | To the Moon and Pack Again

media:group.media:title: Christina Koch Visits NC State University | To the Moon and Pack Again
media:group.media:description:
From Aug. 24-25, 2026, NC State University proudly welcomed NASA astronaut Christina Hammock Koch home to her alma mater. During her visit, Chancellor Kevin Howell announced that Koch Hall has been named in her honor.
Koch holds three degrees from NC State. In April 2026, she and her crewmates flew farther from Earth’s bounds than anyone in human history on the Artemis II mission.
Read more about Koch's visit to campus: http://ncst.at/cRGB50ZHWbm
Video visual description: Christina Koch speaks from behind a lectern to a crowd gathered on the Oval at NC State's Centennial Campus for her Welcome Home Celebration. As her remarks play, montage footage shows Koch meeting students, posing with Gov. Josh Stein and Chancellor Kevin Howell, tasting Howling Cow's limited-edition Howl at the Moon ice cream, and speaking with children. When she mentions her love of rockets, NASA footage highlights her Artemis II mission and views of Earth from space. Chancellor Howell addresses the crowd, accompanied by clips of Mr. and Ms. Wuf dancing with the Power Sound of the South and her mural at the Free Expression Tunnel. Following the announcement naming Koch Hall, Koch walks to the stage. She then poses with the Koch Hall banner and is later shown taking selfies with students at Stewart Theatre, and belaying students on the rock wall at Carmichael Gym.

entry.title: Astronaut Strategies for College Students — A Conversation with Christina Hammock Koch

media:group.media:title: Astronaut Strategies for College Students — A Conversation with Christina Hammock Koch
media:group.media:description:
Astronauts learn psychological strategies that help them stay grounded in space — strategies you can use to survive exam season, build resilience and transform stress into success. Hear firsthand how Christina Koch navigated ambition, doubt and risks throughout college and in pursuit of her dream career.
----- ℹ️ Around the Moon and Pack Again || This event is part of Christina Koch's visit to the NC State campus Aug. 24–25, 2026. Koch holds three degrees from NC State: a B.S. in electrical engineering and physics and an M.S. in electrical engineering. She served as Mission Specialist I of NASA’s Artemis II mission. The crew launched on April 1, 2026 from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Alongside fellow NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, Koch splashed down April 10, 2026 off the coast of San Diego, completing a nearly 10-day journey that took them around the moon and 252,756 miles from home — the farthest any humans have been from Earth.

entry.title: The Launchpad Effect: How Public Higher Education Propels Us Toward a Brighter Future

media:group.media:title: The Launchpad Effect: How Public Higher Education Propels Us Toward a Brighter Future
media:group.media:description:
“Most kids probably dream of becoming an astronaut. I was just the one that never grew out of it.” – Christina Hammock Koch
When public higher education opens doors for curious students, like NASA astronaut and three-time NC State graduate Christina Koch, they can go farther than humanity has ever gone. Koch and Chancellor Kevin Howell will be joined by leading NC State faculty and students for a conversation that will explore what it takes to achieve a big dream, solve a grand challenge or answer a question that has never been asked before — and how NC State, as a land-grant institution, empowers us to Think and Do for the betterment of North Carolina and our world.
